name: sol_basics_math_11
description: Unchecked overflow/underflow or division-by-zero in inline assembly arithmetic
question: The source file in `source` contains an inline assembly (e.g. Yul) block that performs arithmetic operations such as div, mod, mul, add, or sub on values used in security-relevant logic, without any preceding or surrounding check that a divisor is nonzero or that the operands cannot overflow/underflow, so that assembly silently returns 0 for division/modulo by zero or wraps around on overflow/underflow instead of reverting, potentially corrupting balances, shares, or other critical state. This excludes assembly arithmetic where the inputs are already bounds-checked in high-level code before entering the block, or where overflow/underflow is provably impossible given fixed, small, hardcoded constants.
criteria: An assembly block computes div(a, b) or mod(a, b) with b coming from user input or external calls, with no check that b != 0 before or inside the assembly block
An assembly block computes mul(a, b) used for share/amount calculations without any check that the result did not overflow relative to a or b
An assembly block computes sub(a, b) representing a balance or amount decrease without verifying a >= b beforehand, allowing underflow to wrap to a huge value
An assembly block computes add(a, b) for accumulating balances or totals without verifying the sum does not overflow the storage type before writing it back
